- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1-2% for next 3-5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of decline after peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day average) to reduce noise before forecasting.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.00/1.00), model tends to overfit; apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast amplitude by 10–20% if sentiment swings >2x in 3 days.
